text:
Recent evidence supports separating history dependence from order dependence. A RecSys 2026 study found pairwise history models outperforming tested Transformers on four of five benchmarks; useful older history therefore need not imply higher-order sequence reasoning. Its Transformers were SASRec variants, so this motivates BERT4Rec diagnostics without establishing BERT4Rec-specific behavior. [Authors’ research summary](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling). A September 2026 attribution preprint covering BERT4Rec reports unreliable raw attention explanations and stronger faithfulness from GradientSHAP/Integrated Gradients. Its separately trained masking probe is incompatible with this task’s single-model constraint; borrow the concern about masking artifacts, not the additional model. [Temporal attribution benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201).

Suggested controlled suite, inferred from these findings: hold targets and candidate sets fixed on training-history prefixes; compare deleting the latest k interactions against repeated count-matched random deletion and older-only deletion. Separately shuffle older history while preserving the recent suffix, then shuffle the suffix while preserving older history. Include unchanged-input controls, deterministic evaluation, and explicit handling of deletion-induced position changes. Preserve BERT4Rec’s masked-target semantics; append the reserved MASK after each perturbed prefix, left-pad, and read the final nonpadding position. The original method uses Cloze training to prevent bidirectional target leakage. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690).

Report paired target-rank deterioration, reciprocal-rank change, and HR@10 change; aggregate repeated perturbations within users and bootstrap users for uncertainty, separately by category. Greater damage from recent deletion than random deletion suggests disproportionate recent-context reliance; shuffle effects indicate positional sensitivity. Neither establishes user intent, causal preference change, or higher-order reasoning. Treat these as behavioral probes of the existing model, with no fitted auxiliary predictor or score fusion.
